From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: ACME - RAG eval follow-up and next steps

Hi Alex — great to meet you and the team today. Quick recap and next steps below.

Recap:
- Use case: customer-facing support assistant that must ground answers to internal knowledge base + product docs.
- SLOs you mentioned: sub-300ms median token latency for fast queries, and <5% critical hallucination on high-confidence answers.

Model recommendations (short list):
- redwood-opt-instruct-7b-q4: good balance of quality / cost for early pilot.
- redwood-rlhf-3b: lower cost, strong instruction-following, useful for higher-throughput routing.
- For highest-quality reranking: use a cross-encoder variant (text-reranker-large) as the final reranker on top candidates.

Benchmarks / prompt sets:
- Shared Drive link with our benchmark CSVs and example prompt sets: https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-benchmarks (attached summary + CSV).
- Attachment: redwood-rag-eval-summary.pdf — contains baseline MRR, grounding precision @K, and latency numbers for the cluster we used.

RAG-specific config guidance (starter):
- Retriever: dense with FAISS HNSW, embedding model = redwood-embed-768.
- Candidate pool: top_k = 50 retrieval, then rerank top_10 with cross-encoder.
- Reranker: cross-encoder (text-reranker-large) provides best grounding precision at cost of CPU; for lower-cost option use a lightweight bi-encoder reranker.
- Grounding thresholds: consider answer_acceptance_threshold = 0.7 (probability calibrated via evals) and a fallback policy to respond with "I don't know" or offer a link if confidence < threshold.
- Metrics to track: grounding_precision@K, grounding_recall@K, MRR, hallucination_rate (manually labeled sub-sample), and average latency per request.

Next steps:
1) Technical deep-dive with your engineers — propose Wed 6/16 or Thu 6/17 (30–45m).
2) We'll share a pre-call eval package (prompt sets + sample queries + suggested coarse eval script).
3) If pilot is greenlit, we'll propose a lightweight scope & pricing draft.

I'm looping in our solutions engineer to prep the technical artifacts.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference

Hi Alex / Laura — confirmed Wed 6/16 10:00am PT for a 45m technical deep-dive. Calendar invite and video link sent separately.

Pre-call package (shared):
- redwood-rag-eval-summary.pdf (attached)
- benchmark-results-20260612.csv (attached)
- Example prompt sets + eval script: https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-benchmarks
- HubSpot deal record: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/12345 (ACME pilot draft attached).

Short answers to your clarifying Qs:
1) top_k tradeoff: increasing to 100 improves recall on long-tail but linearly increases CPU for reranker and end-to-end latency. We recommend starting at 50 and running a 1k-query sweep at 100 to measure delta; if recall lift > 6–8% it's often worth the cost.
2) reranker lift: on our June benchmark, cross-encoder -> improved grounding_precision@5 by ~12–18% vs bi-encoder (depends on domain). I'll have Connor bring exact numbers.
3) sampling for hallucination_rate: 500 query labels gives a noisy estimate; 1k+ labeled queries is preferred for stable estimates across intents.

We'll send a short pre-call checklist (sample queries + quick eval instructions) before the meeting so we can show live numbers. Looking forward to it.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
